features.rule: candidates: confirmed trained-encoder features ordered by added development AUROC over log volume, one per correlated family; nodule: stable trained-encoder features with nodule enrichment >= 3 that are not confirmed candidates, taken in order of enrichment while cycling over the peak region (inside, 0-4 mm, 4-10 mm); random: stable random-weight features, confirmed first, then by nodule enrichment; shuffled (one per site): the first candidate's case values permuted within each split, images unchanged; every feature is active (case value > 0) in at least minimum_active_confirmation development patients

examples.rule: case value = maximum feature activation over positions inside the nodule or within 4 mm of its surface (one record per patient, profile members). Generation uses training patients (discovery), validation uses development patients (confirmation). High = largest case values; low = for each high example in order, the unused patient with the nearest log nodule volume among those at or below the split's low_quantile of case values

render.rule: three orthogonal planes through the nodule mask centroid in radiological orientation with physical aspect; generation images add a lung-window row with the feature activation (trilinear on the canonical input grid, colour scale fixed per feature by the largest value over its generation examples); validation images show only the lung and mediastinal rows, identical for every feature

specificity.rule: per site, a fixed panel of development patients (ordered by a hash of the record identifier among all validation patients of that site) is scored against every non-shuffled label of the route; a specific label ranks the panel by its own feature's case value better than by the other features' values

prompts.layout: The image is a CT region of {window_mm} mm centred on a target lung nodule. Columns: axial, coronal and sagittal planes through the nodule centre in radiological orientation (yellow letters mark patient right R, anterior A and superior S). Row 1: lung window (level -600, width 1500 HU). Row 2: mediastinal window (level 40, width 400 HU).{overlay_row} The white bar is 10 mm.
prompts.overlay_row: Row 3: lung window with a coloured overlay showing where one image feature of a model responds; brighter yellow means a stronger response and no colour means no response.
